description: Snowscript UDFs - a scalar LANGUAGE SQL UDF with a Snowflake-Scripting block body (every expectation measured on a real account): all three delimiters plus the unquoted block form (unquoted expressions/queries stay syntax errors); real block semantics (first RETURN wins, LET/DECLARE, IF, WHILE, EXCEPTION, no-RETURN yields NULL); bare parameter references with shadowing; NULL arguments and RETURNS NULL ON NULL INPUT; RETURN cast to the declared type with call-time failures for uncastable values and semi-structured return types; the restricted body language (no DML/queries/EXECUTE IMMEDIATE/CALL/SELECT INTO/cursors/subqueries under either bind style/UDF calls/recursion - built-ins allowed) with Snowflake's own wording; the procedure-side bind split; scope hygiene between UDFs and calling procedures; no UDF may call a block-bodied one while non-UDF callers all may; per-row evaluation; and the untouched expression/query body paths. Converted 1:1 from ddl/ScriptingUdfBodyTest (now retired).

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE sub_src (v INTEGER)

CREATE FUNCTION f_caller(n INT) RETURNS INT AS $$ BEGIN RETURN f_helper(n) + 1; END $$

CREATE FUNCTION f_caller3(n INT) RETURNS INT AS $$ BEGIN LET x INT := f_helper(2); RETURN x; END $$
CREATE FUNCTION f_fact(n INT) RETURNS INT AS $$ BEGIN IF (n <= 1) THEN RETURN 1; END IF; RETURN n * f_fact(n - 1); END $$
CREATE FUNCTION f_abs(n INT) RETURNS INT AS $$ BEGIN RETURN ABS(n) + 1; END $$

$$
DECLARE
  zz INT DEFAULT 7;
BEGIN

END
$$
